info.description:
Multi-tenant SaaS for insurance agency offices (KPM).

Every failure uses one envelope — `{ error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }` — and every `code` has a row in `docs/02-specs/api/error-catalog.md`. **Branch on the code, never on the message.**

A resource in another tenant answers `404`, not `403`: a `403` would confirm the id exists.

refreshToken.description: Only for non-browser clients. A browser sends the httpOnly cookie set at login and should omit this entirely.

token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Expires in 15 minutes.

pronoun.description: Yours to set. It appears in the coaching commitment sentence your leader reads.

reason.example: This branch already trades under KPM 0417.
reason.description: Kept, and sent back to whoever asked. A refusal with nothing to act on is not an answer.

slug.description: Derived from the name by the console and editable there. Unique among companies that have not been deleted; a clash is refused with COMPANY_SLUG_TAKEN.

code.description: Stable and semantic. Upper-cased on the way in, and never changed afterwards.

displayOrder.description: Junior first. Presentation only — nothing references it.

status.description: Archiving retires a rung without deleting it. Nothing is ever deleted here.

code.description: Unique within the company. Prefixes agent codes.

timezone.description: v1 runs on a single time zone. Asia/Jakarta is the only accepted value; omit it and the office inherits the same value from its company (ADR-0016).

payload.description: The whole payload for this kind. Shape depends on the kind: `activity_taxonomy` is `{ categories, types }`, `lead_pipeline` is `{ statuses }`, `ratio_set` is `{ ratios }`.

reason.example: Their activity types were saved with a duplicate code and cannot be fixed from the screen.

email.description: The account to make Owner. It must already exist — create one at /register or with POST /auth/register. Email is what a Super Admin normally knows.

toMembershipId.description: Required when action is `reassign`. The membership their reports move to.

details.description: What is specific to this failure — the permission that was missing, the field that was wrong, the code already taken.

requestId.description: On every response and in every log line. Quote it to support.

initials.description: Derived server-side, so every avatar agrees.

orgLevelCode.description: The rung of the company's ladder this person stands on (P4-T9). What a role badge is drawn from, and what a hierarchy permission is compared against.

hierarchyRole.description: The v1 enum. Read by the services that sort and group; no longer an authorisation input.

directCount.description: What makes somebody a leader (OD-23) — the rung does not.

impersonationReadOnly.description: A support session that may look and not touch (§3.13). False outside a session, and false inside one a second Super Admin has approved to write.

impersonatedBy.description: The real Super Admin, when this is a support session.

mustChangePassword.description: They are on a password somebody else generated. Every route but this one, change-password and logout answers 403 until it is replaced (P3.6-T4).

permissions.description: Resolved from the database on every request.

companyId.description: The insurer, named and identified. The id travels because somebody whose branch is not on the platform has to say which company they would belong to, and the directory is the only place a newcomer can learn which companies exist. It names no office and leaks nothing an outsider could not read from the list itself.

url.description: The shareable form. The QR encodes exactly this.

leaderMembershipId.description: The leader this request names — which is who the joiner joins if it is approved with no destination, and whose sub-units are the destinations on offer. For a leader reading their own inbox this is always themselves. For the Owner or an Admin reading the office queue it differs per row, and the screen cannot render the destination list — or say plainly where an approval sends somebody — without it.

forLeaderMembershipId.description: The leader whose sub-unit this is. A leader's inbox holds only requests addressed to them, so one list served every row. A tenant admin's inbox is the whole office, where each row names a different leader — and `approve()` validates the destination against **the requested leader**, not the actor. So a single list was not merely imprecise there, it was unusable: every choice it offered was refused with `422`.

code.description: The identity. Every activity log, ratio formula and goal target holds this, and nothing can change it — see `tenant-config.md`.

appliesToOrgLevelCodes.description: The rungs that may log this, **inherited from its category and never stored here**. Empty means every rung.

displayOrder.description: Presentation only, and reorderable. Nothing reads it back.

version.description: The domain's version, bumped when what the office counts changes. Not a reorder.

appliesToOrgLevelCodes.description: The rungs this section is a question for. **Empty means every rung**, and it cascades to every type inside — a type has no applicability of its own.

numerator.description: Activity type codes, summed. Never the prototype's item numbers.

origin.description: `platform` rows were provisioned — their numerator and denominator are fixed so that two offices’ figures mean the same thing. `office` rows are the office’s own and free in every respect.

appliesToOrgLevelCodes.description: Ladder rung codes. **Empty means every rung.**

standardNumerator.description: The formula this office was provisioned with (ADR-0024), or `null` on a ratio it created. What a divergence is measured against, and what the screen shows an Owner they moved away from.

divergesFromStandard.description: The formula no longer matches what this office was seeded from (ADR-0024). A display and support caveat: nothing is excluded from any comparison on account of it, because a platform comparison computes the seeded formula rather than reading this row.

displayUnit.description: How to write `benchmark` for a reader. `percent`: × 100 to one decimal (15.0%). `decimal`: two decimals (0.30). `points`: ± percentage points (±30 points). Always `points` on a `band` ratio.

code.description: What every lead holds. Renaming the label leaves this alone.

isTerminal.description: The stage that closes this pipeline, and what gates marking a lead successful. Exactly one per pipeline — a property, not "the last one in the list".

code.description: The identity. Never changes, never reused.

skillCode.description: The skill it teaches. **Its category is that skill's**, never stored here.

publishState.description: Whether agents are offered the module **at all**. Not when: that is the office's own publish. A draft never reaches an agent.

description.example: Structured modules — tracked here, and later in your Skill Tracker.
description.description: The subtitle an agent's category page shows.

training.description: The training taxonomy agents are offered: active categories and skills, and **published** active modules only (P5-T1). A draft never reaches an agent.

version.description: The highest version across everything above — one number to compare rather than three collections to reason about. It moves when what the office counts changes, and not on a reorder, because a reorder rebinds nothing.

id.description: Empty when nothing has been saved yet.

version.description: The version this is, or will be once published.

publishedVersion.description: What new offices are seeded from today. Null when nothing is published.

officesBehind.description: How many of this company's offices were built from an older version of this kind — including those built from the platform defaults because nothing of it was published.

officesUnrecorded.description: How many were created before provisioning recorded this kind, so whether they are current is not known. Counted apart from `officesBehind`, which only counts offices known to be behind (P5-T12).

publishedVersion.description: What agents are on. 0 when nothing is published.

workingVersion.description: The highest live row version. Informational — **not** a change detector: a created row starts at 1, and an edit below the maximum or an archive leaves it where it was. Read `hasUnpublishedChanges` for that.

hasUnpublishedChanges.description: Whether any row has been created, edited, archived or restored since the last publish, judged by which rows are present at which version. A reorder is not a change. True for an office with nothing published.

fiscalYearStartMonth.description: The month the office's financial year starts, 1–12 (P4-T5). Stored and shown now; read by the period computations in Phase 14.

completesWhen.example: the hire has saved any goal since joining this office

live.description: Whether an evaluator exists yet. While it does not, a leader ticks the item by hand and the tick is recorded as manual; once it is live, no role may tick it.

version.description: What a hire's activation records at creation.

published.description: The version hires starting now are given. `null` before the first publish.

draft.description: The office's working copy. `null` when nothing has changed since publishing.

windowDays.description: The office's activation window. Shown beside the checklist; changed in Branch info.

canChangeRole.description: Whether this viewer may change *this* person's role. Sent rather than inferred, because the rule is a server rule and the screen should not carry a second copy of it that can drift.

total.description: What makes somebody a leader (OD-23) — the rung does not.

layer.description: Depth **within this projection**, one-based — the number on the column label. Not the same as `depth + 1`, and that is the whole point of sending it. An AB two layers down the office is *Layer 1* of their own tree, because AC-1 says layer one is you. Computing it here keeps one coordinate frame: a client that subtracted its own root's depth would be a second one, and the two disagree the moment a projection has roots at different depths.

ownerHasLeft.description: The owner has been removed from the office. They are still named — they really are the recorded owner, and a blank would look like a fault. But an Owner reading the list needs to know the group has nobody running it, so the flag travels and the screen says both.

canChangeRole.description: May **this viewer** move this person between Agent and AAB. A direct leader may; so may the office. Decides what is offered, never what is allowed — the API refuses regardless.

canPromoteToAb.description: May they involve the AB rung. The office only — a leader cannot make somebody their own peer.

canRemove.description: May they remove this person. False for yourself, for the office root, and for anybody already removed.

agencyBuilders.description: How many of them hold the AB rung.

slug.description: Derived from the name by the console, and unique among companies that are not deleted.

defaultCurrency.description: Fixed for v1 (ADR-0016). Every office inherits it.

defaultTimezone.description: Fixed for v1 (ADR-0016). Every day boundary in every office of this company resolves here.

line.description: The line a spreadsheet shows, header counted.

willCreate.description: Zero whenever anything is wrong: it is all or nothing.

kpmId.description: Null for a platform-level action, which belongs to no office.

actorUserId.description: The real actor. Under impersonation this stays the Super Admin.
